newly_closed: the annihilator of a product of cyclic quotients R/(e_i) is the intersection of the principal ideals (e_i)
for D = product_i e_i and A = intersection_i (e_i), the finite bounds (D) <= A and A^(card i) <= (D) hold without ordering the coefficients
over a principal ideal ring, a chosen generator a of A satisfies a divides D and D divides a^(card i)
the product ideal (D) and the intrinsic annihilator A have equal radicals, including the empty-index case
the actual localized cutoff-one relative quotient has annihilator equal both to the selected coefficient-ideal intersection and to the denominator scalar colon
the two finite Satz-VIII divisibilities and their radical consequence are instantiated for the actual localized first Smith quotient
limitations: This is the finite localized Smith-algebra kernel of the opening of Satz VIII. Mathlib v4.31 does not supply a divisibility-ordered canonical elementary-divisor family through the selected Smith API, so the annihilator generator is used as an intrinsic replacement for a greatest coefficient. The selected product is not identified with Hentzelt's primitive resultant form R^(i), the generator is not identified with a normalized historical E^(i), and no coefficient ordering, normalization, choice independence, determinant-norm/resultant identification, primitive descent from Frac(P[x_3,...])[x_2], historical unbounded-tail identification, later stage, equation (33), or equation (34) is asserted.
